note: SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURES. Not real measurements. Values are chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand.
semantics_ref: Latency: DerivedLatencyStats.from and Confidence.of at phase-3b-measurement-engine@727b2a91. Jitter: PHASE_4_CROSS_CUTTING_TECHNICAL_DECISION_CONTRACT.md D4-3 (pairs of adjacent successful, same-method, warm, same-network samples; samples used = members of at least one valid pair).

sample_format.t: send time offset in ms from series start (must be non-decreasing, otherwise the series is unordered evidence)
sample_format.v: latency in ms (present when the sample succeeded)
sample_format.fail: failure label (present when the sample failed)
sample_format.cold: true for a cold-connection sample (default false, meaning warm)

fixtures.description: Ten stable samples alternating 20 and 21 ms. Consistent, so the illustrative latency confidence is High.
Ten wide samples alternating 10 and 110 ms. Spread 100 exceeds half the 60 ms average, so the illustrative latency confidence is Medium.
Single sample. Latency aggregates with Insufficient confidence. No pair exists, so jitter is null.
Two samples. Latency confidence Insufficient (fewer than 3). One pair exists.
Timeout sequence: every sample fails. No latency aggregate exists (insufficient evidence) and jitter is null. A timeout must never be averaged as a value.
Timeout then recovery: fail, 20, 22, 21 ms. The failure contributes nothing and starts no pair.
Gapped series 10, 20, FAIL, 30, 40. The failure breaks adjacency. Two pairs exist and all four samples belong to a pair.

known_implementation_divergence.detail: DerivedJitterStats.from seeds the first sample of a pair only when no delay has been collected yet, so the first sample of a later, separate run of pairs (30 here) is dropped from sampleCount, pdvRangeMillis and sourceMeasurementIds. Expected implementation output at that commit by hand trace: sample_count 3. Confirm by running this fixture against the Kotlin implementation.

fixtures.description: Gapped series with the extremes in the second run: 50, 60, FAIL, 10, 20. Correct range uses all four samples (10 to 60 = 50).

known_implementation_divergence.detail: Same cause as FIX-LAT-009. By hand trace and a line-by-line transliteration (not execution of the Kotlin), the implementation would report sample_count 3 and pdv_range 40 here because sample 10 is dropped.

fixtures.description: Network change mid-series: samples 1 and 2 on network 1, samples 3 and 4 on network 2. The pair across the change is not counted.

latency.reason: Aggregating latency across two networks is a labeling hazard, see harness rule H-AGG-1

fixtures.description: Cold then warm samples: one cold-connection sample followed by three warm samples. The cold sample uses a different method id and never pairs.

latency.reason: Cold and warm samples are different methods and must not be aggregated together, see harness rule H-AGG-1

fixtures.description: Unordered series: send offsets 0, 200, 100. Unordered evidence is rejected for jitter. Latency still aggregates over the values.
